key_insight: The authors produce RXL-RADSet, a radiologist-verified synthetic multi-RADS benchmark, and use it to perform a head‑to‑head evaluation of 41 open-weight and proprietary language models, demonstrating that well-tuned small open models can viably compete on RADS assignment tasks when measured on standardized synthetic data.
problem_solved: Automating RADS assignment from free-text radiology reports is hindered by complex guideline logic, strict output-format requirements, and a lack of standardized benchmarks spanning multiple RADS frameworks and model scales.
method: Create RXL-RADSet: a synthetic, radiologist-verified dataset that covers multiple RADS frameworks and encodes realistic report variants and structured RADS labels.
Enforce output-format and guideline constraints in prompts/evaluation to mirror clinical RADS assignment rules.
Conduct head-to-head benchmarking of 41 models (open-weight small language models and at least one proprietary model) measuring label validity and assignment accuracy across RADS frameworks.
impact: Provides a reusable, validated benchmark to compare models on clinically relevant RADS tasks, enabling practitioners to select, tune, and validate smaller open models for deployment while ensuring output format and guideline compliance.
visual_elements: Overview diagram of RXL-RADSet: number of RADS frameworks covered, synthetic report examples, and radiologist verification step
Pipeline flowchart: synthetic report generation → constrained prompting → RADS label extraction → automated + radiologist validation
Bar/strip chart comparing validity and accuracy across model sizes and between open-weight vs proprietary models (41-model panel)
Confusion matrix or Sankey showing common misassignments between RADS categories to highlight failure modes
paper_title: Multi-RADS Synthetic Radiology Report Dataset and Head-to-Head Benchmarking of 41 Open-Weight and Proprietary Language Models
paper_authors: Kartik Bose, Abhinandan Kumar, Raghuraman Soundararajan, Priya Mudgil, Samonee Ralmilay
